title: Cognizant Lands Centene Healthcare Deal Worth Up to $1 Billion, Marking AI-Led Comeback
excerpt: The multi-year contract reunites Cognizant with a major US health insurer after nearly a decade, leveraging TriZetto software and agentic AI to automate claims and billing.
body:
Key Takeaways
  • Cognizant's deal with Centene could be worth up to $1 billion, reviving a long-term partnership.
  • The contract utilizes TriZetto software and Agentic AI for automating healthcare processes.
  • This marks Cognizant's second mega deal in two weeks, following a similar contract in communications.
  • Cognizant's large deal count has increased from 17 to 29 over the past year.
  • Analysts will scrutinize the Centene deal's margin profile during Cognizant's Q2 earnings report.

Back in Centene's Corner

Cognizant Technology Solutions has secured a multi-year technology services deal with US health insurer Centene Corp that could be worth up to $1 billion, according to a report by Moneycontrol citing people familiar with the matter. The contract, valued at well over $500 million, includes a mix of contract renewals and new business — effectively bringing Cognizant back as Centene's key technology partner after nearly a decade.

The two companies share a long history. In 2014, Cognizant signed a $2.7 billion, seven-year master services agreement with Health Net. That deal was upended when Centene acquired Health Net in 2016, leading to a restructuring of the original contract. Under the revised arrangement, Cognizant continued providing selected technology and business process services but lost the scope of the original engagement.

The latest win reverses that trajectory.

"Both the mega deals were originated by us, and not from RFPs. These are transformation deals. The deal that we closed is approximately around a billion dollars."

— Surya Gummadi, President, Cognizant Americas

AI at the Centre of the Deal

Cognizant is expected to deploy its TriZetto healthcare software platform alongside its recently launched Agentic AI frameworks — Cognizant Flowsource and Agent Foundry — to support Centene's operations. The technology will automate key healthcare processes including medical billing, claims processing and customer service functions.

The deal is seen as a major validation of CEO Ravi Kumar's strategy of expanding AI-driven healthcare services and automation across Cognizant's client base. Kumar, who took over as CEO in January 2023, has been pushing the company to use AI-generated productivity savings to fund new transformation work for clients.

"We are leveraging AI to unlock productivity and use that unlocked value to fund transformation and innovation again powered by AI," Gummadi said in a recent fireside chat with Bank of America. "And this is resonating extremely well with our clients."

Two Mega Deals in Two Weeks

The Centene contract is Cognizant's second mega deal — defined as worth more than $500 million — in the past two weeks. The first, an unnamed deal in the communications, media and technology (CMT) space, was announced by Gummadi at the same Bank of America event.

Notably, both deals were directly originated by Cognizant rather than through conventional request-for-proposal (RFP) processes. The company has increased its large deal count from 17 to 29 in the last year, with an average deal tenure of around five years.

The announcements come at a time when the broader Indian IT services industry has seen a slowdown in large, long-term contracts. For Cognizant, which has struggled to grow organically — acquisitions made up nearly half of its 8.2 percent full-year revenue growth in constant currency terms — the back-to-back wins signal a meaningful shift.

What to Watch

Cognizant is expected to provide more details about the Centene contract when it reports second-quarter earnings on July 29. The deal will be closely watched by analysts for its margin profile, given that healthcare transformation contracts can be initially dilutive before scaling.

For the tens of thousands of Indian-origin professionals who form the backbone of Cognizant's delivery centres in India, the deal reinforces healthcare IT as a durable growth engine — and positions the company's Bengaluru, Chennai and Hyderabad operations for expanded work in AI-led service delivery.
